title: Plasma laws: tip-up over a freed hole slug (INNER cuts); pin inch and G41/G42 programs at the gate

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Part of #672. Two follow-ups from the review of PR #791 (step 2 of the plasma laws), neither blocking that PR.

**1. Tip-up only treats `OUTER` cuts as freed parts.** Step 1 (#675) chose that a rapid is judged against the rings of earlier `OUTER` cuts only (`sim::verify::plasma::judge`, the tip-up loop filters on `CutRole::Outer`). A hole's slug is cut free just the same, and can tip up into the torch when a later rapid runs over it (UM10720 §1.4.2 names the dropped slug). Judge rapids against earlier `INNER` rings too - a slug smaller than the kerf-width drop gap falls away, so a small-hole rule (`small`) or a slug-size floor may apply; decide and record it.

**2. Inch documents and G41/G42 programs through the gate are not pinned.** The laws run in mm on the torch-centre moves, and the only unit-dependent part is `describe()` through `units::len`; a control-compensated program carries the same centre-line moves. Add a `plasma_gate` case (or two) for an inch document (the not-judged line and a refusal in inches) and a `control_comp` op.

**Done means:** a rapid over an earlier hole's slug is a `TipUp` finding naming the hole (pinned in sim `plasma_laws` and read through `plasma_program`), with the slug-size decision in `docs/decisions/`; `plasma_gate` pins an inch document and a G41/G42 program through `verification_report`.

Labels intended: P2, effort:high, area:sim, source:agent.
